It also introduces students to the basics of newsgathering, reporting, copyediting, and ethical news practices. In addition to acquainting students with reporting, editing, and designing, the course will train students to pitch their work to news media organisations. Objectives: ● To understand the roles and responsibilities of a journalist ● To help students understand news values and critically evaluate information ● To build information databases and develop a research mindset ● To encourage habits that will help students excel at investigative journalism ● To develop an understanding of the ethical roles of journalists ● To make class participants more informed and critical consumers of news media Unit 1: Newsroom Structure and Contemporary Journalism News Values Unit 2: Newsgathering Techniques Unit 3: Developing Stories / Ideation Unit 4: Developing Story Ideas into Printable Stories Unit 5: Specialised Writing Areas Evaluation : Total Marks: 100 (Final written exam 60 marks; 40 marks internal assessment) Suggested Readings: ● Hodgson, F.W. MCJ-101 -Print Journalism Practical Course Brief: The paper will help students learn through practical experience. The aim is to expose students to situations and ideas that they will have to face in newsrooms and in the ﬁeld. Through hands-on training, students will be introduced to the nuances of ideation, news reporting, writing and editing for print and online
